messages.subject: RServe and R with proxy configuration
messages.subject_clean: RServe and R with proxy configuration
messages.body_plain:
Hi,
we communicate with R through RServe in a proxy environment but we have 
some problem with R network communications. I don't manage to localize 
the problem at this moment, I send this mail in hope someone could help us.
The application runs on the 3 OS: Win, Linux, Mac and we need to have 
the ability to call install.packages() through RServe even if the client 
OS has a proxy network configuration.

For Mac and Linux, we launch R through RServe and set the proxy using 
Sys.setenv(http_proxy="http://user:password at proxy.example.com:8080"); 
(through RServe too)

Through RServe (on Linux):

install.packages("xxx", dependencies=TRUE, repos="http://cran.rstudio.com");

hangs up until the R time out is reached and then returns:

Warning: unable to access index for repository 
http://cran.rstudio.com/src/contrib

But:

print(Sys.getenv("http_proxy"));

through RServe returns well the proxy configuration.

Calling:

install.packages("xxx", dependencies=TRUE, repos="http://cran.rstudio.com");

directly in R works.

I made a very lot of tests through RServe and the strange thing is that 
it worked one time on Linux (if I remember well).
Do you think it's possible there is some kind of conflict between the 
RServe <=> R communications and the R <=> Internet configurations or is 
it 2 different things?
I think about for example some extra arguments that RServe would pass to 
R to communicate with it ?

Thank you very much in advance for any help or clues.
Sebastian

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I had a similar user case with Rserve in my application which was solved with the following recipe. Maybee a solution for you, too.
 
"...Another reason is that are sitting behind a proxy and you can't connect to the repository, see:
 
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/4832560/how-do-i-tell-the-r-interpreter-how-to-use-the-proxy-server
 
Try the last described solution in the post:
 
"If you want internet2 to be used everytime you use R you could add the following line to the Rprofile.site file which is located in R.x.x\etc\Rprofile.site

utils::setInternet2(TRUE)"

Here another post suggesting the same - but with: setInternet2(TRUE) -:
 
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9024466/r-connect-via-proxy-server?lq=1[http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9024466/r-connect-via-proxy-server?lq=1]
 
.............................."

Best regards

Marcel

messages.subject: Re: RServe and R with proxy configuration
messages.subject_clean: RServe and R with proxy configuration
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
thank you Marcel for your help. Actually we need to manually define the 
proxy configuration, not to activate the system proxy management.
About our issue, it now seems to work very fine through RServe. It came 
from the "http://" string that was missing in the Sys.setenv().
For information this code has been tested on the 3 OS and seems to work 
(through RServe too):

Sys.setenv(http_proxy="http://proxy.univfc.fr:3000");

And here is a summary on what I found about the proxy conf in R:

- Win => "internet2" forces the system proxy configuration usage
- Linux => by default R uses the env var "http_proxy" if exists
- Mac => idem but the Mac network manager does not create an 
"http_proxy" env var, you can set it to R through launching arg or 
Sys.setenv()
             => you can retrieve the system proxy using "networksetup"
             => you may also "export" the "http_proxy" before running 
R/RServe (not tested)

Thanks for reading.
Sebastian
